candidates.title: Why Blizzard made WoW Classic after saying no
candidates.narration: J. Allen Brack rejected World of Warcraft Classic, then announced it. At BlizzCon 2013, fans asked for the original game back, and his answer is still quoted: "You think you do, but you don't." Four years later, he unveiled it. Blizzard's stated reasons for the wait were the cost of running two MMOs at once, and technical problems. Neither explains the change of heart. What happened in between was a fan server. Nostalrius ran the original game unofficially, with 150,000 active players. Blizzard shut it down in 2016. Then Blizzard met the Nostalrius team, and they shared their code. I think fans built Classic before Blizzard did. You think you do. Turns out they did.

candidates.title: Blizzard told WoW fans they were wrong
candidates.narration: Blizzard told WoW fans, "You think you do, but you don't." That was J. Allen Brack, then World of Warcraft's production director, at BlizzCon 2013, to fans asking for the original game. Strange thing to say, because four years later Brack announced exactly that: WoW Classic. Blizzard says the blocker was cost and tech. But something else happened in between. Fans built it themselves. An unofficial server called Nostalrius had 150,000 active players when Blizzard shut it down in April 2016. Over 200,000 people signed a petition. Blizzard then met the Nostalrius team, who handed over their code. I think that's what changed Brack's mind. Classic won PC Game of the Year in 2019. They did.

candidates.structure: (iv) tiny story: wanted, obstacle, turn, outcome
candidates.title: The WoW fan server Blizzard shut, then needed
candidates.narration: Blizzard shut a World of Warcraft fan server, then met its team. The server was Nostalrius. Its players wanted the original WoW, the one later expansions had changed, and Blizzard wouldn't run it. So they ran it themselves, unofficially, and drew 150,000 active players. In April 2016, a Blizzard cease and desist ended it. Instead, a petition passed 200,000 signatures, and ex-WoW team lead Mark Kern delivered it to Blizzard's president, Mike Morhaime. Then came the turn. Blizzard met the Nostalrius team, and they shared their code. A year and a half later, Blizzard announced WoW Classic. I think Blizzard owes that server more than it ever admitted. It shut down the prototype.
candidates.answer: Nostalrius handed Blizzard its code

candidates.structure: (i) contradiction, rule out, reveal, verdict
candidates.title: Was GTA San Andreas's CJ underpaid?
candidates.narration: CJ's voice actor once called Rockstar "culture vultures." For years, fans read that as proof Rockstar had underpaid Young Maylay for GTA San Andreas. It fit a pattern people already believed. Michael Hollick, who voiced Niko Bellic in GTA IV, reportedly got about $100,000 flat for 15 months. Then, this month, Maylay went on Ned Luke's show, The Final Mission, and said the pay story was false. He knew the terms when he signed. And Rockstar sent him bonuses after launch that he didn't expect. I'll take his word over the internet's. He's the one who signed the contract. Whatever "culture vultures" meant, by his own account it wasn't about the paycheck.
candidates.answer: Maylay says the pay story is false and Rockstar sent bonuses
